extracted.intended_audience: unemployment insurance agents, UIC administrators, and policymakers involved in benefit adjudication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for Agents I and II in administering unemployment insurance: determining claimant eligibility, evaluating availability/active job search, making and notifying decisions, and handling special cases (sickness, maternity, labour disputes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Active job search / availability obligation (sec. 55(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimants must 'search actively for a job' as part of the concept of 'availability' and fulfil the requirement of sec. 55(8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent I must explain to claimants the sector of the job market the search should cover, the frequency of search attempts, and how they can be substantiated. The obligation applies to all claimants except those receiving sickness, maternity or retirement benefits. UIC brochures encourage claimants to register with CMC and other agencies, consult newspapers, write to and visit potential employers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active Job Search Program participation and form submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain claimants whose job skills are in particular demand must submit, at regular intervals, an 'active job search statement' recording details of their search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement is primarily an instrument of control (verification of availability/willingness) rather than assistance. Claimants who refuse to produce one risk being disentitled under sec. 25(a); refusal to comply with written directives aimed at helping them may lead to disqualification under sec. 40(1)(c). Once subject to the program a claimant remains so until employed again or vacancies cease to exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable-efforts standard and 'reasonable interval' (Ricard principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimants are only required to prove they have made 'such efforts as were reasonable in the circumstances' — evaluation should be related to each claimant's particular circumstances rather than a uniform minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice the UIC uses a formula for staff: first three weeks only jobs in own occupation and normal earnings; skilled workers then get one week extension per year of experience up to a maximum (3–16 weeks total). After that, search must expand to other occupations with a progressive lowering of earnings (5% less per week) down to the prevailing rate; Agents are instructed not to inform claimants in advance of these calculations to avoid strategic behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: No uniform minimum contacts unless locally justified
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms and pamphlets do not specify a universal minimum number of weekly contacts for 'ordinary' claimants; District Office may add mention of minimum contacts for certain classes or areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no minimum is shown, the District Office assesses the value of contacts in relation to demand for the claimant's skills within a reasonable distance. Prior determination of a uniform minimum can be an unwarranted extension beyond sec. 55(8) per Ricard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof/substantiation of job search
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary claimants are asked to keep a list of employers approached (date, type of employment sought, names of interviewers, reply); program participants must complete the active job search statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pamphlet states it is not necessary to obtain employer certificates. Ordinary claimants confirm continued availability on the claimant's report form sent every two weeks. Active job search statements are required every two weeks and must be certified by the claimant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and limits of 'suitable' employment
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Suitable' employment excludes jobs vacant due to a labour dispute and, for jobs of the same kind, only counts if rate of earnings and working conditions are at least as favourable as under collective agreement or 'good' employers; sec. 40(3) makes different kinds suitable after a 'reasonable interval'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unemployment insurance is not intended to create a cheap labour pool; claimants have no absolute right to refuse different-kind jobs once the reasonable interval has elapsed. Suitability is judged by earnings and conditions compared to collective bargaining standards or recognized employers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent I responsibilities in applicant interaction and implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent I must ensure claimant fulfils sec. 55(8), explain necessary searches, provide forms, process registration with CMC, and implement his decision through Regional Payment Centre forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disallowing a claim, Agent I must explain reasons and inform claimant of right to appeal; a form letter follows oral rejections. When allowing a claim, Agent I explains benefit calculation, weeks entitled, date of first cheque, and claimant's report card mechanics; gives active job search statement if applicable and forwards registration forms to CMC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claimant's report card handling and timing importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimant's report cards (sent with benefit cheques) report paid work, earnings, training, dependants, return to work/school, and include claimant's certification of ability and availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents must explain importance of proper and timely submission: cards must not be mailed too early (before end of the period covered) or too late (which may delay payment). Regional Payment Centre processes cards by computer and notifies District Office of changes that may affect benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II overarching authority and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II has 'original jurisdiction' over most benefit matters, broader decision-making authority than Agent I, and responsibility for both preliminary and subsequent control (recovery of overpayments, penalties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent II exercises almost total decision-making authority (except Regional Office exceptions) and must balance simplicity and speed with consistency and accuracy. The role includes assisting claimants per sec. 106 and providing 'personalized' service within limits set by efficiency and uniformity requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II job description: inform claimants of rights and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II must inform claimants of their rights and obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as item 1 in the UIC Manual job description; part of the Agent II's frontline duties to explain claimant entitlements and duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II job description: claimant assistance (settle problems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II settles problems that arise in dealings between claimants and the UIC (claimant assistance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes addressing misunderstandings, clarifying requirements, and guiding claimants through procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II job description: employment assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II helps claimants find work through advice and information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Has access to job documentation and labour market knowledge to refer claimants to appropriate opportunities; this duty is distinct from being a placement agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II job description: financial assistance advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II helps claimants through advice and information to overcome financial difficulties caused by unemployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory role only; not a welfare agency providing direct financial services beyond unemployment benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II job description: appeal assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II informs and helps claimants in the exercise of their rights of appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must explain appeal procedures and assist claimants in pursuing appeals where appropriate (pamphlet 'Appeal Procedure' available).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II job description: examine special benefit applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II examines applications for special benefits (sickness, maternity, retirement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent II handles contentious or complex special-benefit claims, including premature maternity applications and assessing entitlement to ordinary benefits up to maternity-payable period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II job description: verify benefit calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II verifies the calculations made to establish the amount of benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsible for checking accuracy of monetary determinations before implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II job description: review ability and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II decides whether a review is required of claimants' ability and availability for work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitors ongoing eligibility and may initiate reviews when circumstances change or when files indicate potential issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II job description: determine entitlement with regard to law and individual situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II determines entitlement to unemployment insurance benefits in the light of the Act, the Regulations and the caselaw, with due regard for individual situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses UIC Manual and the Digest of Benefit Entitlement Principles (caselaw abstract) but often relies on experience and judgment; must weigh statutory/regulatory text and precedent with claimant-specific facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II job description: notify and implement decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II notifies claimants of decisions and how they will be implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes explaining implementation steps and ensuring administrative follow-through (computer inputs, payment centre notifications, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II job description: explain unfavourable decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II explains reasons for decisions unfavourable to claimants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear explanations to reduce appeals where possible and to reassure the public; such explanations are a key part of claimant assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II job description: track implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II keeps track of the implementation of his decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures payments, recoveries, or control actions are actually carried out and monitors outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contentious-file examination priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II focuses on entitlement and grounds for disqualification, prioritizing circumstances under which employment was terminated and questions as to claimant availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two types of contentious files: those 'contentious by nature' (quitting, misconduct, special categories) and those that 'become contentious' after contact; Agent II checks Agent I work, elicits further information, and may contact claimant/employer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical certificate handling for sickness benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical certificate from treating physician provides conclusive proof of sickness/disability but not duration of incapacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent refers to 'Medical Yardsticks' to determine duration; the certificate remains confidential on file and inquiries are to be referred to the issuing physician.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling premature maternity applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For premature applications, Agent II must assess entitlement to ordinary benefit up to the point maternity benefits become payable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claimant proves availability and is not disqualified for other reasons, she may receive ordinary benefits until maternity benefits begin; if pregnancy complications prevent work, sickness benefits may apply until maternity benefits start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification through claimant and employer contacts; fraud protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: If facts about termination are in doubt, Agent II questions claimant, obtains claimant's version, and contacts the employer; statements are entered in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fraud is suspected (falsification of termination reasons), Agent II requests Benefit Control Unit investigation. All information gathered is recorded and used in decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing voluntary quitting and setting disqualification length
rubrics_metrics.description: When claimant quit voluntarily, Agent II explores justification and may vary disqualification length depending on seriousness or extenuating circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent exercises discretion to calibrate penalty period in light of the facts presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability assessment for restrictive claimant conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II assesses the extent to which a claimant's self-imposed restrictions on type/hours/place/pay of work deny availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimants placing unduly restrictive conditions are not considered available; this assessment links to reasonable-interval rules that broaden suitable employment over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job referral process and consequences of refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II may mention jobs available through the CMC and suggest claimant visit CMC; refusal to follow advice can be grounds for disqualification (sec. 40(1)(c)) or disentitlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision on the claim may be held pending notification from CMC about placement attempt results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active Job Search Committee occupational selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Each District Office's Active Job Search Committee identifies occupational categories in which demand is plentiful and defines related occupations to be systematically subject to the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee composition: Chief of Operations, Supervisor of insurance services, an Agent II and a Benefit Control Officer; uses data sources (CMC, media, private agencies, company contacts, labour market analyst) to choose occupations and claimant subgroups (age, residence, disabilities) for systematic inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of UIC Manual and Digest and the role of experience/judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents should use the UIC Manual and the Digest of Benefit Entitlement Principles as sources but rely heavily on familiarity, experience, and judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digest contains caselaw abstracts and an analytical index; Agents rarely have time to consult these fully, so practical experience and an instinctive ability to reach the heart of a contentious application are emphasized, while guarding against routine mechanical decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent II role in labour disputes and umbrella determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: On learning a labour dispute has begun or may occur, Agent II compiles detailed files (companies affected, negotiators, workers involved, nature of dispute, dates/times, picket behaviour, strike pay sources) and recommends to Regional Office which classes of workers the disentitlement grounds (sec. 44) should apply to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once Regional Office makes an umbrella decision, Agents II apply it to individual benefit applications in affected districts; must determine who is directly interested in the dispute and whether picket actions prevent work (affecting entitlement).
